title: Every registered wrapper writes through the existing discipline and adds nothing to it
statement: Each registered creation, mutation, activation and stage-attestation tool performs its write through the existing locked, atomic, validated implementation rather than reaching the filesystem itself, and every wrapper - read or write - resolves the content root through the shared resolver rather than deriving one. A wrapper adds only the Pi-facing schema and the rendering of a result: no validation rule, no id allocation, no trace rule and no write path is restated in it. Every result is structured, a refusal is returned as data rather than thrown as prose, and neither carries a credential, a credential-derived value or an absolute user path.
notes: ⚠️ REOPENED 2026-09-14 (F114): EVERY RESULT WAS STRUCTURED FOR KILN AND EMPTY FOR THE MODEL. EVD-0102 observed handler results returned through a recording stub and the session registry, not the provider-facing tool content. No wrapper result or refusal was model-visible. `rendered()` in `pi-package/extensions/kiln.js` returned `{output, details}` with no `content`, and Pi sends a tool result without `content` to the provider as `(no tool output)`. A real `/kiln-start` session measured it on 2026-09-14: `kiln_project_status` executed without error and the provider received exactly that placeholder. The historical evidence and its link are kept unchanged. This criterion returns to pass only on supplemental evidence that the provider-facing tool message carries the rendered result. ⚠️ RESTORED TO PASS 2026-09-14 ON EVD-0106: commit 81f69a9 returns every result as text content equal to its rendering, and CI run 34812083727 observed it at the handler boundary for all 28 tools and in a real provider request for kiln_capability. ⚠️ NARROWED TO TSK-0044. This criterion accepted TSK-0044 AND TSK-0045, which do not depend on each other, so neither could be finished without the other's work also being done - and its wording is about mutation wrappers, which are TSK-0044's, while TSK-0045's adapters mostly write no planning content at all. TSK-0045 now has its own criterion for what its adapters must do. ⚠️ THE WRAPPER IS A BOUNDARY, NOT A SECOND IMPLEMENTATION. Everything it calls already exists in `lib/` with the lock, the atomic write, the schema validation and the id allocator behind it. A wrapper that re-derived the content root, or re-checked a rule, would be a second answer to a question that already has one - which is how the two drift apart without either being obviously wrong.
